meta.title: Silver — SGGW computer science student club
meta.description: The computer science student club at SGGW. We build the apps the campus uses.

hero.title: The computer science club at SGGW.
hero.lead: Got Plan WZIM on your phone? We built it. The next one takes a few people and a semester — you could be one of them.

steps.heading: How it works

items.title: Join the Discord
items.body: It's all there: projects, meetups, people. Introduce yourself in one sentence.

items.title: Pick a project or pitch your own
items.body: Get into something that's already running, or bring an idea and find two people for it.

items.title: Build it over the semester
items.body: A small team, your own pace. Every so often we meet up in person in room 3/79.

steps.hackathons: We go to hackathons too. HackArena 3.0, March 2026: 4th place in the final.

projects.heading: Projects
projects.lead: Two of our apps are in the stores with over a thousand downloads each. The rest is on GitHub.

build.heading: What we build, and with what
build.what: Some of what we build fixes problems we run into at university ourselves — that's where the timetable app and the campus map came from. The rest happens because someone wanted to try a new technology, or do a familiar thing their own way.
build.how: We don't have one stack. We pick the tools that fit the project, and we're happy to try new ones — sometimes before anyone calls them stable.

join.heading: Join
join.lead: You don't need to know how to code yet. Wanting to build something is enough.
join.threshold: Join the Discord, introduce yourself, pick a project. That's where we post the in-person meetups too.
join.stripProjects: We build this kind of thing in small teams. Pick a project that's running, or bring your own.
join.stripHistory: The list is still growing. What we're building now, and when we meet, is on the Discord.

companies.lead: A seven-person student team that ships apps to the stores.
companies.who: The Silver .NET computer science student club at the Faculty of Applied Informatics and Mathematics, SGGW. We build mobile and web apps — for students on campus and for ourselves.
